the dispatch safety gate cannot tell 'this row writes here' from 'this row mentions this path', so an honest spec is refused and a vague one passes. Censused 2026-09-02 on d49964e: 20 of 125 spec files return verdict refuse. Causes: state-schema.json 8, diagnose 6, evidence/ 5, claims 5, design/ 3, then singletons. The first two causes are legitimate -- that IS the claim surface. But 'diagnose' mostly matches the FILENAME bin/perry-diagnose rather than the /perry diagnose pipeline the hook means; 'design/' matches a spec CITING design/DESIGN-NNN rather than writing into it; and 'evidence/' matches a spec declaring its own evidence output, which every dispatched row has. Live instance: TASK-263's spec was refused solely because its Files in scope and Deliverable name perry/evidence/2026-09/TASK-263-result.md, the file the row exists to produce. The pressure this creates is the dangerous part -- the cheapest way to pass is to stop naming the path, and .perry/hook.md says in its own words that rewording to pass is the one thing a gate must never reward. Same defect class as impl_refs counting a design id by text match (TASK-282): a literal matcher standing in for intent. Candidate fixes: distinguish a write-target section from a citation, or scope the fragments that name Perry's own state dirs to foreign roots only

dispatching a subagent WITHOUT worktree isolation lets it switch the shared working tree to its own branch, so the PMO's concurrent writes land there too -- and a 'git add -A' in the agent's commit would sweep them into its code commit. Observed live 2026-09-02: TASK-247 was dispatched as a claude-subagent with the instruction to create coding/task-247-config-predicate; the shared tree is now ON that branch, and every PMO write made after dispatch (TASK-212 next, TASK-282 depends, TASK-263 spec and evidence, two intake rows) is uncommitted on it. Nothing is lost and git makes it separable by path -- PMO state is perry/ plus .perry/events.jsonl, the agent's work is bin/ and tests/ -- but the separation is manual and it is only obvious to whoever knows both happened. work/reference/dispatch.md tells the agent to work on a feature branch and says nothing about tree isolation, while git-boundaries.md's whole premise is that one agent must not silently rewrite another's lane. The Agent tool supports isolation: worktree; the dispatch procedure should either require it or state why the shared tree is acceptable
